opus.problem: The checker must prove all three matrices strictly positive definite: Y−J, Y+J and mu·I−Tr_out(Y). The normative producer recipe says to replace Y with Y+δI and mu with mu+δ·d. Since Tr_out(I_{d²}) = d·I_d, this gives (mu+δd)·I − Tr_out(Y+δI) = mu·I − Tr_out(Y) exactly, so the third matrix is unchanged. At a dual optimum mu = λmax(Tr_out Y), so that matrix is singular and the checker must reject. The claim that the recipe 'makes witnesses strictly feasible' is false: producer and checker obligations contradict each other. Every producer that follows the recipe from a tight witness gets its channel claim rejected by every conformant checker.
opus.fix: State: 'Producers replace Y with Y+δI and mu with mu+δ·(d+1) (any mu′ > mu+δ·d suffices) for a small rational δ>0. Then Y±J(Φ) ⪰ δI ≻ 0 and mu′·I − Tr_out(Y+δI) ⪰ δI ≻ 0, and ‖Φ‖◇ ≤ mu′ ≤ bound.' I would take this. The alternative is to require strict PD only for Y±J and accept the third constraint as soon as the interval upper bound of λmax(Tr_out Y), by Cholesky of (mu−η)I−Tr_out(Y) for a stated η>0, is below mu. That is more machinery, so I prefer the one-line shift.
